**Roughly a dozen cycles already reached this exact "nothing new" verdict
today** (git log and this file's own head show PM check-ins and operator
cycles at 11:4x through 15:1x all independently confirming the same
exhausted state). Running a thirteenth identical reconfirmation would have
added nothing issue #42 does not already say, so instead went looking for
ground nothing had swept: `ops/cold_read_ledger.py`'s lanes only ever
covered `ops/*.py`, `ops/*.js`, `site/assets/js/*.js` and
`mobile/quest-app/lib/*.js`. `photos/*.py` (4 files, built 2026-10-14/15,
twice independently security-reviewed per PHOTOS-API.md) had never been
read by this mechanism, and a security review hunts for attacker-triggered
gaps, not an ordinary-use correctness bug.

**Found a real defect reading `photos/store.py` directly.**
`add_photo`/`delete_photo`/`save_analysis` did read-modify-write on one
session's `meta.json` with no lock. `ThreadingHTTPServer` gives every
request its own thread, so two overlapping requests on the same session (a
before and an after photo sent back to back is the ordinary case) could
both read the file before either wrote it back; the second write silently
erased the first writer's new photo entry. The `.jpg` itself still lands on
disk, orphaned, while the caller who uploaded it was already sent `201`.
Proved directly against the pre-fix code with a forced, deterministic
interleave rather than timing luck: both uploads returned `201`, only one
id survived in the listing afterward.

**Fixed.** One re-entrant lock per session (`Store._lock_for`, created only
once a session directory is confirmed to exist, so a flood of guessed or
invalid session ids cannot grow the lock table unboundedly) and a new
`_authorize()` helper (read + token check, no write) let `open()`,
`add_photo`, `delete_photo`, `save_analysis` and `delete_session` each run
their full read-through-write as one locked critical section. Re-proved
fail-then-pass in `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py` (33 to 37 checks): the
new cases force a second request to actually block mid-`open()` while the
first still holds the lock, then confirm both uploads survive.

**Turned the lesson into a gate, not just a fix.** Added `photos/*.py` as a
fifth lane in `ops/cold_read_ledger.py` and ledgered all four files
(`store.py` fixed, the other three clean), so this is a one-time gap, not a
recurring one. `PHOTOS-API.md` and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22 updated to
the new 37-check count; `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 14 records the full
account.

**Verified after:** `test_photos_service.py` 37/37, `test_build_photo_
check_data.py` 5/5, `test_cold_read_ledger_stale.py` 7/7, `test_gate_cold_
read_handoff_not_stale.py` 26/26, `check_urls.py` 213/213, `audit_pages.py`
clean, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` 165 documents,
`link_graph_report.py` 0 orphans. No price, product or shipped page
touched; `photos/` is still undeployed (Phil's own call,
`OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22), so this fix reaches zero live customers today
and closes the gap before his deploy decision could expose it. IndexNow
not applicable.

**Went well:** not repeating a thirteenth identical full reconfirmation;
checking the cold-read ledger's own lane list against what the repository
actually contains rather than trusting "N of N ledgered" at face value.

**Did not go well:** nothing this cycle; the defect found was pre-existing
and pre-deploy, with zero live impact.

**Changing next cycle:** none for the operating loop; the new lane closes
this specific gap. Worth a standing habit, not a rule: when a directory is
added to the repository, check whether it needs to join an existing sweep
lane rather than assuming existing lanes already cover it.

## 2026-10-15, scheduled operator cycle (video_cleanalong.py's import-order hazard found and fixed)

**Did:** Unshallowed and fast-forwarded cleanly onto origin/main (which kept moving under the hourly-brief/PM-check-in cadence; re-fetched and fast-forwarded twice more during the cycle). Reconfirmed independently rather than cited: all 10 GitHub issues unchanged (decision/blocked-on-art), 0 open PRs, `ops/cycle_signal.py --check` SAME, `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` 0, production `deploy-verdict.json` current (build `c36cb2794e581473` matches `site/build-id.txt`, 0 `site/**`/Dockerfile commits since its `checked_at`), `inbox_agent.py --apply` ran clean (no mail credential in this sandbox, expected). Chased the one red "Checks" run visible in GitHub Actions (runs #2159-2161, `gate_nightly_log_ordering`) to its job log rather than trusting the 08:4x PM check-in's own claim: confirmed those three ran against pre-fix commits and the real fix (`fae87a97b`) was already in flight: genuinely stale, not newly red, matching the claim.

Found and fixed a real defect instead of re-deriving "nothing to do" again: cold-read of `ops/video_cleanalong.py` (new 2026-10-14, 0 log mentions, the oldest un-ledgered candidate `cold_read_ledger.py --next` names). It forced YouTube wide mode on the shared `video_zone` module by appending `--wide` to `sys.argv` before importing it, relying on `video_zone` reading `sys.argv` only once, at its own import time. Proved directly in a throwaway process: importing `video_zone` narrow first, then `video_cleanalong`, left `vz.WIDE` False and `W,H` at 1080x1920 despite `--wide` sitting in `sys.argv`, because the already-cached module never re-read it; `vz.page()`/`vz.shot()` would then silently render portrait frames that the final `ffmpeg scale=1920:1080` stretches into a distorted 16:9 upload, with no error anywhere. `gate_tests` runs every `test_*.py` as its own subprocess (confirmed in `preflight.py`'s own `gate_tests`, one `_run_bounded` call per file), so this ordering never manifests there today, and nothing yet imports `video_cleanalong` from another module (grepped), so there is no live exploit path, only a latent one for whatever batch script combines it with `video_zone` next.

**Verified:** fixed by setting `vz.WIDE`/`vz.W`/`vz.H` directly on the imported module instead of mutating `sys.argv`, which works regardless of import order and leaves `sys.argv` untouched for every other module in the process. Fail-then-pass proved directly against both mechanisms in the adversarial order (old: WIDE stays False; new: WIDE forced True, argv unchanged). `ops/tests/test_video_cleanalong.py` extended with the two checks that prove it (6 to 8), re-run clean standalone. `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on both touched files. Ledgered as fixed in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json` with the full account. Full `preflight.py` re-run after the edit; see this entry's own HANDOFF-FILES line and the commit this lands in for its verdict.

**Went well:** the standing cold-read fallback found a genuine, previously-unflagged, demonstrated defect in a brand-new file on the very first candidate, the same shape as the last two cycles' own finds (`rotate_nightly_log.py`, `cycle_signal.py`).

**Changing next cycle:** none; the standing fallback is working as designed.

Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, `STATUS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`. `ops/cycle_signal.py --check` reported SAME against the last recorded clean pass, and a dedicated search agent independently confirmed `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 2 through 9 are genuinely exhausted (every row Done, Phil-gated, or closed by decision) and `ops/cold_read_ledger.py` is saturated (199/199). Rather than stop there, looked for a real defect nobody had named: `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` had grown to 8.1MB / 57,105 lines / 2,795 entries, never rotated since the file existed. Three `preflight.py` gates plus STEP 1 of this very prompt each read the whole file on every single run to look at a handful of recent entries, a real and compounding cost (the same shape issue #42 names for the cadence generally, just never traced to this file).

**Fixed:** new `ops/rotate_nightly_log.py` moves entries older than a 14-day window into `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG-ARCHIVE.md`, verbatim, nothing deleted. Date resolution searches each heading for a `YYYY-MM-DD` anywhere in it (about a quarter of entries carry no leading date) and inherits forward from the nearest earlier dated entry otherwise; checked directly against the real file before trusting it (137 of 2,795 entries would have been mis-dated by one day using a leading-only match). Applied once this cycle: live log is now 780 entries / 2.24MB (was 2,795 / 8.06MB). New `gate_nightly_log_not_oversized` in `preflight.py` (WARNING, matching its two neighbours) re-fires if it drifts past retention+7 days again, so this cannot silently regrow. Also extended `ops/cold_read_ledger.py`'s `_mention_counts()` to scan the archive too, since otherwise its own ranking signal would have silently gone stale the moment entries left the live file, the exact "source corrected, downstream not updated" shape this repository keeps finding elsewhere.

**Verified:** `ops/tests/test_rotate_nightly_log.py` and `ops/tests/test_gate_nightly_log_not_oversized.py` both fail-then-pass proved (new gate confirmed to actually warn on a real oversized log and stay silent on a clean one). Ran the new gate directly against the real file both before and after rotation (warned before, clean after). `gate_ops_python_syntax`, `gate_ci_path_filter_covers_preflight_inputs`, `gate_checks_excludes_generated_files`, `gate_nightly_log_ordering`, `gate_nightly_log_no_duplicate_entries`, `gate_cold_read_handoff_not_stale` all re-run directly against the rotated file, clean. Existing `ops/tests/test_nightly_log.py` and `ops/tests/test_cold_read_ledger_stale.py` still pass unmodified. A full `preflight.py` run completed clean before this change (every gate passed, 30 standing sandbox-limitation warnings, no real FAIL) and a second full run was started after this change; it was still running in the background past this entry's own write (known to take up to ~600s), so that specific full-suite confirmation is reported as started, not yet complete, rather than claimed.

**Did:** Unshallowed, attached to main, `merge --ff-only` clean (61 commits fast-forwarded, no unrelated-history symptom). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` in full, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the last several `NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entries. `ops/cycle_signal.py --check`: SAME against the last clean snapshot, meaning sections 2-6 of the backlog were already exhausted and GitHub's 9 open issues (checked directly) unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`. `ops/inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential. **The real finding, checked rather than assumed:** `linkedin-drafts.yml` (LinkedIn is this site's largest identified traffic source, per `GOALS.md`) has a push-triggered fallback specifically built to catch a late cron, gated by a once-a-day commit ledger. Its `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` branch, though, sent unconditionally on the assumption cron fires at most once a day. It does not fire ON TIME once a day: `gate_scheduled_delivery_phase` already measures this same workflow landing 156 minutes past its own promised time. When the delayed schedule run finally executes after the push fallback has already sent for the day, both paths send. Read directly from `git log --grep='LinkedIn drafts: advance rotation'`: 8 of the last 28 days carried 2 or 3 real send commits in one day, including every day from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-12 straight. `bluesky-drafts.yml` and `social-drafts.yml` (copied from the same template) carry the identical shape and the identical pattern: 8 of 13 and 8 of 28 tracked days respectively. Phil has been receiving 2 to 3 copies of the same morning drafts on most recent days, on every distribution channel this site actively drafts for.

**Fixed:** all three workflows now send unconditionally only for `workflow_dispatch` (a deliberate manual run); `schedule` falls through to the same "already sent today" commit-ledger check `push` already had. Simulated all six gate branches directly in a throwaway shell script before touching the real files (schedule-on-time, schedule-delayed-after-a-push-send is the bug case, push-before-target, push-fallback-empty-ledger, push-fallback-already-sent, manual-dispatch): all six produced the correct `send=yes`/`send=no`. New `gate_schedule_fallback_race` in `ops/preflight.py`, fail-then-pass proved directly (planted the old pattern in a throwaway file, watched it fail by name, confirmed the real fixed files pass) and against `ops/tests/test_gate_schedule_fallback_race.py` (7/7 cases, including the real committed workflows). Wired into `main()` beside its sibling `gate_push_fallback_ledger_honest`.

**Verified:** full `preflight.py` (fast) run to completion, not cited from a prior cycle: every gate passed, 31 warnings, all previously-diagnosed environment-access limits, no new FAIL. `ops/affiliate.py --check` (165 documents) and `ops/fix_dashes.py --check` (0/0) both clean after. YAML syntax and `ast.parse` on the edited files both clean.

**Went well:** the fix was found by actually reading git history instead of trusting that "the schedule always eventually fires" (the exact assumption the 2026-09-30 sibling fix to this same gate step already named as luck, not evidence) — the duplicate-send pattern was sitting in plain sight in three files' own commit logs the whole time.

**Did not go well:** none this cycle; a real, currently-active, multi-day defect on the one channel this business depends on for traffic went unnoticed through roughly 50+ prior cycles that each independently reconfirmed "nothing new unblocked" without checking whether the thing already shipped was behaving honestly.

A gate proves the code looks right; it does not prove the workflow has been behaving right in production, which this one had not for at least two weeks.

## 2026-10-12, scheduled operator cycle: took the cold-read handoff, found and fixed two real defects in build_image_prompts.py, gated

**Finished?** Yes. Checkout arrived shallow and detached; `git fetch --unshallow`, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only` onto `origin/main` landed clean, 575 commits, no unrelated-history symptom. `ops/cycle_signal.py --check` reported CHANGED (only `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`, a low-risk bookkeeping row), so ran the real verification rather than skip it. GitHub's 9 open issues unchanged (2 `P0`, rest `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none mine to pick up per CLAUDE.md 0.5). `ops/inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing. `ops/affiliate.py --check`: clean, 165 documents.

**Took the queued handoff**: second-pass cold read of `build_feed.py`, `build_icons.py`, `build_id.py`, `build_image_prompts.py`, `build_kitchen_deck_pdf.py`. Four read clean (feed regenerates current at 30 entries; icon arc geometry, PNG dimensions and manifest/HTML icon references all check out, cannot execute directly since Pillow is not installed here, standing sandbox limit; build-id hashes git's index deliberately rather than working-tree bytes and matches; kitchen deck PDF's sheet hash matches the live print sheet, and its upstream generator regenerates idempotently).

**The find, in `build_image_prompts.py`, two defects:**

1. `main()`'s `if want_tier:` treated `--tier 0` as no filter at all, because `0` is falsy in Python. The docstring and a long code comment frame tier 0 as "the only number that matters... the whole first batch", so this is exactly the invocation someone would run expecting just the 6-image starter batch; instead it silently wrote all three tier files, 228 prompts. Proved directly: before the fix, `--tier 0` wrote 3 files/228 prompts; after, it writes 1 file/6 prompts. Fixed to `if want_tier is not None:`.

2. The committed `content/images/prompts/tier-1-prompts.md` and `tier-2-prompts.md` were stale against `content.json`'s own text, which had been swept from British to American spelling (`unlabelled`→`unlabeled`, `grey`→`gray`, `labelled`→`labeled`, `tyre`→`tire`, `metre`→`meter`, `Jewellery`→`Jewelry`) but never regenerated afterward. This is the exact "source corrected, shipped artifact never re-derived" shape `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 7 and 8 name as the dominant defect class here. `gate_no_british_spellings_shipped` does not catch it: by design it scopes to `site/**/*.html` and `ops/cardtext/build_*.py`, the things a visitor or Phil-the-card-author actually reads, and these prompt files are an internal image-generation intake queue, never shipped. Regenerated both files from the fixed generator (spelling only; diffed the full change to confirm nothing else moved).

**Fixed and gated:** refactored `build_image_prompts.py`'s `main()` to extract `all_items()`, `render_tier()` and `by_tier()`, so the generator has one source of truth instead of two (the old version duplicated the render logic inline in `main()`, which is what let a defect in it go uncompared against anything). New `gate_image_prompts_tiers_current` in `preflight.py`, mirroring `gate_feed_current`'s regenerate-and-diff pattern, calls those same shared functions and fails if any of the three committed tier files disagrees with a fresh run. Proved fail-then-pass directly (planted the old British spelling back into tier-1, watched the gate fail by name citing the right file, restored, reran clean) and in new `ops/tests/test_gate_image_prompts_tiers_current.py` (5/5 cases, including a missing-file case and a real-corpus-size sanity check). Registered in `main()` next to its sibling `gate_image_prompts_tier0_count_honest`; `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP` mapping updated to list both gates for `build_image_prompts.py`.

**Verified:** `ops/tests/test_gate_image_prompts_tiers_current.py` 5/5. Direct `--check`/equivalent runs of all five touched/reviewed generators clean (`build_feed.py`, `build_id.py`, `build_kitchen_deck_pdf.py`, plus the new gate itself). `ops/affiliate.py --check` clean. Ran a full `preflight.py --fast` in the background; it was still inside its documented multi-minute `gate_tests` tail when this entry was written, so that tier is reported as **unchecked, not passing**, per CLAUDE.md 0.4, even though every gate directly relevant to this change (the new gate, its sibling, `gate_no_british_spellings_shipped`) was individually exercised and came back clean. Cold-read ledger updated for all five handed-off files, `build_image_prompts.py` marked `fixed` with the full account.

**Went well:** the second-pass cold-read handoff mechanism surfaced two real, previously-invisible defects in a file a first pass had marked clean; both were only visible by actually running the generator's two code paths (`--tier 0` and an unfiltered run) rather than reading the source and trusting the prior note.

**Did not go well:** none new.

**Changing next cycle:** none; the handoff mechanism and the new gate are both working as designed.

**Next for the operator:** second-pass cold read of the next oldest-dated tier: `build_microzone_coverage.py`, `build_mobile_corpus.py`, `build_printpack.py`, `build_product_schema.py`, `build_pwa.py`.

## 2026-10-12, scheduled operator cycle: fixed two real indexation_check.py misclassification bugs, PM handoff

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, ff-only onto origin/main, re-synced once more mid-cycle onto a concurrent PM check-in's push, 511 commits). That PM check-in's own handoff named the work: cold-read `ops/indexation_check.py`, the lowest-mention file tied to a live, unresolved priority question (GOALS.md O1: has any individual zone page ever been confirmed indexed).

**Read the file end to end rather than trust its own docstring's "HOW IT REFUSES TO LIE" section, then checked its actual committed output against it.** Two real defects, both confirmed against the live `ops/indexation.json` on disk, not guessed:

1. `classify()` matched `/zones/` and `/articles/` (the sitemap's own hub/listing pages for those sections) by the same substring rule as an individual zone or article page. The ledger's only "zone" entry, ever, was `https://6s-success.com/zones/` itself: the listing page, not a diagnostic zone page. `ops/INDEXATION.md` read "zone: 1" and named `/zones/` under "Zone pages confirmed indexed at least once", stating the exact opposite of the true, still-open answer this file exists to give. Same shape hit `/articles/`.

2. `_domain_urls()` kept any URL containing our domain as a text substring anywhere, not just URLs actually hosted on it. `http://www.bing.com:80/search?q=site%3a6s-success.com`, Bing's own link to its own search-results page carrying our query string, was sitting in "confirmed" permanently, and being additive-only, would have stood as a future trusted canary: a later run could have "proven" it was not blocked by reproducing Bing's own search box link to itself.

Before writing it up as a finding, checked the actual cause rather than the symptom (CLAUDE.md 5d): a `preflight.py` run I had started in the background was still writing to `site/**/*.html` while I ran the generators in the foreground, racing the same files. ## 2026-10-10, scheduled operator cycle, correction (a preflight gate_tests failure this cycle was a race with concurrent git surgery, not a real regression)

**Correcting a scare from this same cycle, written before it could mislead a later one.** After pushing the nightly_log.py atomic-write fix (fd9d954fe), ran a second full `preflight.py` in the background to confirm the final state, but kept working the git merge (checkout, rebase --continue) on the same tree while it ran. That run reported `1 gate(s) failed`: `gate_tests` named `test_gate_affiliate_trigger_citation_current.py` failing with `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError`.

**Verified before believing it.** Ran that one test file standalone against the settled, pushed tree: `OK: gate_affiliate_trigger_citation_current, 5/5 checks pass`. Ran a third full `preflight.py`, this time touching nothing else while it ran: `every gate passed, 29 warning(s)`, clean.

**The lesson:** a backgrounded preflight run reads real files from the working tree as it goes; running `git checkout`/`rebase --continue` concurrently on the same tree can catch a JSON file mid-rewrite and report a false test failure that looks exactly like a real regression. Per CLAUDE.md 0.4, this is recorded rather than quietly dropped, so a future cycle that sees this same test named in a failure does not skip re-verifying it standalone first. No gate needed: the fix is procedural (do not run git surgery and a backgrounded preflight against the same tree at once), not a code defect, and this is a first occurrence, not a recurring pattern.

No files changed by this entry beyond itself and the command deck.

**Cold-read finding, fixed:** the tool's main() wrote NIGHTLY-LOG.md by opening it directly in "w" mode, which truncates the file before the new content is written. A crash mid-write (disk full, kill, container eviction) between truncation and completion would have corrupted the one file this operating prompt calls the only reliable account of what has been tried, the exact failure mode this tool exists to prevent for a different defect class. Fixed with a write-to-temp-file-then-os.replace atomic rename, so the real path is only ever replaced by a fully-written file.

**Proved the fix and the test, not just asserted them.** Added two cases to ops/tests/test_nightly_log.py (5/5 to 7/7): one exercises main() end to end against a real file; the other monkeypatches io.open to fail the temp-file write (simulating disk full) and asserts the real log file comes out byte-identical to before, with no stray .tmp left. Confirmed the new test is not theatre by reverting the atomic-write fix, watching it fail with the exact defect it describes ("real log file changed even though the write failed before the rename"), then restoring the fix and watching it pass again, 7/7.

**Went well:** the cold-read ledger surfaced real, fresh, un-exhausted work instead of another "nothing unblocked" conclusion; the fix was proven against its own regression rather than assumed correct from reading the diff.

Fixed: a real pending message on either side now returns 1 first (unchanged priority); only once neither side has anything pending does unchecked get its own code, 2, rather than defaulting to the same 0 as verified-clean. `ops/tests/test_owner_inbox.py`'s own existing "both unavailable" case asserted the OLD behavior as intentional (comment: "must be 0, nothing known to be waiting, not nothing to do"); re-examined against `CLAUDE.md` 0.4 ("unchecked is not passing... report unchecked as loudly as failed") and judged the old reasoning insufficient, since nothing currently calls this script's exit code (confirmed by grep: only `preflight.py` imports the functions directly, nothing pipes `python ops/owner_inbox.py` through `$?`), so there is no existing caller to break and a real future one would be misled by the overload. Updated that case to expect 2, and added a new case asserting the only state that may legitimately return 0 (both checked, both empty). Fail-then-pass proved directly: stashed the code fix, confirmed the updated test fails by name against the real pre-fix `main()`, restored the fix, confirmed it passes (4/4), then found and fixed an ordering bug in my own first attempt at the fix (checking `p is None or third is None` before `p or third`, which would have wrongly returned 2 for the case `p=None, third=[a real message]`) before it ever reached the committed version.

1. **`ops/diagnosis.py`'s `IMPERATIVE_FIRST_WORD` set was still built from the Kitchen deck alone, the only deck that existed when this file was written.** B9 has since authored 19 more room decks, each with its own ACTION CARD steps, and the set was never re-derived against them. The sub-agent found 3 live cases (leave/say/read); independently re-verified by extracting every ACTION CARD step's opening word across all 20 decks and found the real gap is far larger: 108 genuine imperative verbs missing, not 3. Checked each candidate word's actual sentence for mood before adding it (a hazard-list fragment like "Blades. Every blade sheathed..." opens with a noun, not a command, and was excluded), and checked the full candidate set against every real victory text that exists: all 289 ACTION CARD `victory_condition`s across all 20 decks, plus all 114 live `first_15.victory` fields. One word, "dry", had to stay excluded even though it is a genuine imperative elsewhere in the corpus ("Dry the vanity counter...") because this file's own founding example, "Dry basin, two tools standing, nothing lying in water," uses the identical word as a state adjective, and that sentence is the one this file was written to keep passing. Fixed: rebuilt the set (56 to 162 words) and the docstring. New cases 10-11 in `ops/tests/test_diagnosis_schema.py` (the 3-word regression plus all 289 cross-deck victories), fail-then-pass proved against the reverted set. All 5 existing diagnosis test files rerun clean after.

2. **`ops/deploy_freshness.py`'s own comment claimed its 4 discovery pages "reference every fingerprinted asset the site ships." False: `site/downloads/assets/book.css` (written by `ops/build_sample_html.py`, fingerprinted by `ops/fingerprint_assets.py`) is referenced only by the downloads/ sample page, which was not in the list, so it was never compared to production at all.** Independently re-verified and found the bug was worse than "a missing list entry": the referencing page's own href is `assets/book.css`, relative to ITS OWN directory (`site/downloads/`), not to `site/` root like every page already in the list, so simply adding the page would not have been enough. `ops/preflight.py`'s sibling gate (`gate_checker_scope`, meant to catch exactly "an asset no discovery page covers") also could not have caught this, independently confirmed by running it directly: it builds its "shipped" set from `all_pages()`, which deliberately excludes `downloads/` for unrelated reasons (dash/claim gates should not scan the book sample's hand-written prose), so `assets/book.css` was never even in its shipped set to begin with; and even if it had been, the gate's own existence check joined the match straight onto `SITE` (`site/assets/book.css`, which does not exist) instead of resolving it against the referencing page's directory. Fixed: added `resolve_asset_ref()` to `deploy_freshness.py` (resolves an href against the page it was found on, the way a browser does) and the missing discovery page; `gate_checker_scope` now imports and shares the same resolver instead of its own drifted copy, and explicitly scans `downloads/*.html` for its "shipped" set alongside `all_pages()`. Fail-then-pass proved three ways: `test_deploy_freshness.py` (4 resolver cases plus an end-to-end book.css comparison, 12 of 12 passing; raises `AttributeError` against the reverted file, confirming the function did not exist before), `test_gates.py` (new `checker-scope` case, plants a downloads/ page plus its asset, fails on the reverted `preflight.py`, passes on the fix), and `gate_checker_scope()` called directly before/after. The actual divergence this surfaced between `content/book/assets/book.css` and `site/downloads/assets/book.css` (8 lines) is not a bug: `ops/build_sample_html.py` deliberately adds a `.figalt` rule to the shipped copy that the book source does not carry, confirmed by reading that generator directly before treating the diff as a finding.

## 2026-10-09, scheduled operator cycle, addendum: a delegated CI check caught a real, currently-live blocker the first pass of that same check had cleared by mistake

**What happened.** After pushing the cold-read commit above, a delegated sub-agent checking CI status first reported (wrongly) that `publish-image.yml`'s prior FAIL (run #589, commit `170f13d1`, `gate_generator_ownership` failing on `site/sitemap.xml`) was already fixed by later commits, based on running one generator (`ops/build_resources.py`) standalone and seeing byte-identical output. That was a false negative: the gate's own docstring explains why running one generator alone cannot reproduce this class of drift (lastmod/content-hash state depends on the whole 43-generator chain running in order). The same sub-agent then ran the real full chain in the background, caught its own error, and sent a correction: the FAIL was still live at HEAD.

**Fixed.** Ran the real `GENERATOR_OWNERSHIP_CHAIN` directly (43 generators, skipping `build_zone_pages.py`/`build_epub.py` per the gate's own documented sandbox exclusions, no local hero photos or book images here), for real rather than through the gate's own checkout-and-restore wrapper, to see and keep the actual diff. One file changed: `site/sitemap.xml`, 212 URLs to 211. The committed sitemap carried a stray, malformed duplicate `<url>` block for `https://6s-success.com/rooms/laundry-room` (wrong position in the file, lastmod `2026-10-09`, no `image:image` block) alongside the real, correct one (lastmod `2026-10-02`, image block present). Traced to commit `a40c4d2a` (this session's own earlier cold-read fix today), which ran `ops/build_seo.py` standalone to refresh lastmod on 114 changed pages; only one physical file now carries that canonical URL, so this reads as a transient race with a concurrent session's write at the moment that standalone run scanned the tree, not a reproducible logic bug in `build_seo.py` itself (no second source file exists to explain a deterministic duplicate). `ops/build_id.py` rerun (pre-commit hook caught the resulting staleness correctly, exactly as designed).

**Verified:** `check_urls.py` 211/211, `audit_pages.py` 215/0, `fix_dashes.py --check` clean, `affiliate.py --check` clean (165 documents). A background `preflight.py --own` run against the clean, committed tree is this fix's own authoritative confirmation; also triggers a real `publish-image.yml` run (this commit touches `site/**`), which is the actual test that matters.

**Went well:** the sub-agent self-corrected its own false negative within the same investigation rather than letting a wrong "already fixed" stand; delegating CI-status checks surfaced a real, live blocker this cycle's own earlier work had accidentally introduced, closing the loop within the same session rather than leaving it for the next cycle to rediscover.

**Did not go well:** running one generator in isolation to "confirm" a chain-wide gate is a trap worth naming for next time: `gate_generator_ownership`'s own docstring already says not to run `build_seo.py` standalone for exactly this reason, and the first check still did the equivalent (checked one piece of the chain and generalized to the whole chain).

**Changing next cycle:** none; the existing gate caught the original defect correctly. Worth remembering: a generator-ownership verification is only real if the full chain runs, not a sampled piece of it.

Pushed to main (`48a4c07c4`). `site/sitemap.xml`, `site/build-id.txt`. No price or product touched, no new page; the one page's lastmod correction is a dedup, not new content, so IndexNow is not applicable.

**Found and fixed one real, live defect in `inbox_agent.py`.** `classify()`'s delivery-problem and billing checks built `low_t` from the message BODY only, never the subject line. A customer whose subject carries the signal ("Did not receive my download") and whose body is a terse "please check on this" has no delivery-problem or billing words anywhere the classifier looked, so the message fell into the ordinary `draft-for-human` "customer" branch instead of `flag-urgent`, silently losing exactly the urgency CLAUDE.md 0.2 exists to force (the payment-link lesson: a correctly reported problem nobody acts on costs as much as an undetected one, and here the problem would not even have been correctly reported). Reproduced directly before fixing: `classify("buyer@example.com", "Did not receive my download", "Hi, can you check on this please?")` returned `kind="customer"`; same shape for billing with "Refund request please" in the subject. Fixed by folding subject into `low_t`. Fail-then-pass proved twice: via `git stash` against the real module (both cases return `kind="customer"` on the old code, `delivery-problem`/`billing` on the fix), and via two new permanent cases in `ops/tests/test_inbox_agent.py` (now 10, all passing). No new preflight gate needed: `gate_tests()` already globs every `ops/tests/test_*.py` file, matching this file's own established precedent.

**Also re-read `audit_pages.py`, `check_urls.py`, `fill_front_matter.py` and `prerender_shop.py` in full.** All four correctly implemented, each previously-fixed defect (hero-lazy position, the 403-remap docstring, the backslash-repl fix, the lambda-repl fix) still intact, no new defect found. **No new gate added for the zombie run, and that is a deliberate call, not an oversight.** The root cause there was GitHub's own scheduler producing a zombie run, not anything this repository's code did; `gate_keyword_demand_not_stale`'s existing 10-day ceiling is already the correct backstop for exactly this failure mode (this was caught at day 5, before it ever reached FAIL) and a gate cannot fix another system's scheduler. **Then checked the actual CI run on GitHub instead of trusting my own local preflight pass, per CLAUDE.md 0.3 ("a local pass has not proved CI passes"), and it was failing, for real.** `checks.yml` run 1958 (commit `002f62dec`, the :10 cycle's own incident commit) completed `conclusion: failure`, `3 gate(s) failed`. Read the actual log rather than the conclusion field alone: one failure (4 test files, including the two `b284bf7c7` fixed) was already stale, superseded by that later commit; the other two were not. `gate_owner_actions_last_measured_current`: the :10 cycle's own new incident item (item -1, dated 2026-10-09) landed in `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s body while the file's "List reviewed" marker still said 2026-10-04, the exact drift this gate exists to catch, failing on its own author's commit. `gate_send_questions_covers_top_owner_actions`: the same new item -1 was never added to `ops/send_questions.py`'s `BLOCKING` list, so the one email meant to carry every top-ranked owner action to Phil was silently missing the newest and most urgent one. **Confirmed both were still live on current HEAD, not just historically true of an old commit, by running their own test files directly** (`test_gate_owner_actions_last_measured_current.py`, `test_gate_send_questions_covers_top_owner_actions.py`): both FAILed before any edit. (Worth recording for whoever reads this cold: calling the gate FUNCTION directly returns no exception either way, since `fail()`/`warn()` only accumulate into a module-level list; the test files are what actually assert against that list, which is why "I called the gate and it returned" is not the same claim as "I ran its test".)

**Fixed both at the source.** Bumped `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s "List reviewed" marker to 2026-10-09 (the convention that file's own gate exists to enforce, not a rewrite of anything else). Added a new `BLOCKING` entry to `ops/send_questions.py`, in its own words, matching the existing tuple shape and citing `STATUS.md` INCIDENT-002 and issue #40 the same way item -1 itself does. **No new gate needed here either.** Both gates existed, were correctly designed, and did exactly their job: the defect was that the commit which added a new owner-action item never ran them before shipping, not that the gates themselves were blind to this shape. The lesson is procedural, not architectural: the sandbox's own `gate_tests` hang means a local `preflight.py` run can report "0 FAIL" while two real FAILs sit past the hang point, reachable only by a runner with no such limit. Checking CI's actual conclusion, not just firing a push and trusting a clean local fast pass, is what caught this.

**Went well:** checking CI's own logs rather than stopping at a clean local `preflight.py` fast pass, which is exactly the gap that let these two land unnoticed in the first place; verifying the zombie-run theory against a second, same-hour workflow before accepting it, rather than assuming every cron on the account was equally stuck; watching the hand-fired keyword-demand run to actual completion instead of declaring the fix done the moment `workflow_dispatch` returned 204.

Harmless (proven not to block a second dispatch) but a reader of the Actions tab will see it and wonder. Separately: two real CI failures sat on `main` since the :10 cycle's own commit, unnoticed through two further pushes (the :40 cycle's and this cycle's own first push), because nobody between then and now checked `checks.yml`'s actual conclusion rather than this sandbox's own necessarily-partial local pass.

**What happened.** A23's fresh keyword-demand harvest (closing the "snacks" synonym gap, prior entry) committed a re-scored `ops/keyword-demand.json` alongside the content fix. That harvest legitimately moved the "cheap/budget/DIY" cluster's real counts from 29/66/4/99 to 28/66/4/98 (one query left the cluster's autocomplete results entirely between the 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-04 harvests; nothing published regressed). `GOALS.md` still cited the old numbers in its own O1 section. `gate_goals_keyword_cluster_citation_current`'s own test, `test_gate_goals_keyword_cluster_citation_current.py`, checks the real committed `GOALS.md` against the real committed `keyword-demand.json` and correctly failed on GitHub's CI for both the A23 commit and the follow-up docs-only commit built on top of it (confirmed via `get_job_logs` on the completed run: `1 of 383 test file(s) failed`, naming the exact cluster and the exact stale/live numbers).

**Why this was missed locally before pushing.** The local verification before A23's push ran `check_urls.py`, `audit_pages.py`, `fix_dashes.py --check`, `fix_dialect.py --check`, `affiliate.py --check`, `link_graph_report.py` and `audit_visual.py`, all genuinely relevant to the zone-page edit, but never the one test that actually covers a side effect of committing a fresh harvest file: a citation elsewhere in the repo quoting its old numbers. Lesson for next time a harvest file is committed alongside other work: run `gate_goals_keyword_cluster_citation_current()` directly (cheap, no network, no browser) rather than relying on the full preflight run finishing.

## 2026-10-03, PM check-in addendum (18:4x cycle, a concurrent push collided mid-ship)

A concurrent twin cycle (18:3x) pushed its own `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entry and command-deck regen while this cycle's commit was staged. `ops/ship.py`'s rebase step correctly refused the real conflict in the log (`conflict in real source`), but attempting a plain `git merge` to resolve it, then re-running `ship.py`, hit the same refusal again on the second attempt: `ship.py` rebases rather than merges, and rebasing a tree that already contains a merge commit replays the pre-merge commit standalone, reproducing the identical log conflict instead of seeing it as resolved.

Resolved by hand rather than worked around: kept both PM entries (mine on top as the newer one, the twin's 18:3x entry below it, in true chronological order), took origin's committed copies of the three generated deck files, then regenerated them for real with `ops/dashboard.py` rather than trusting either side's stale copy. Verified directly before pushing: `gate_conflict_markers`, `gate_nightly_log_ordering` and `gate_nightly_log_no_duplicate_entries` all called directly against the resolved file, all clean (no stray `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` markers; the nine text hits for those literal strings elsewhere in this file are backtick-quoted prose describing past incidents, not real markers). `git reset --hard` to retry cleanly was denied by this session's own safety classifier (destructive-git), so pushed the already-correct merge commit directly with a plain `git push` instead, which is fast-forward-safe on origin's side and matches STEP 8's own instruction to merge rather than force. `build_id.py --check` current after.

**Worth fixing, not fixed here (scope creep three minutes before the operator):** `ops/ship.py`'s rebase-conflict handling has no path for "I already resolved this with a merge"; it will reproduce the same conflict on retry. A future cycle should either teach it to detect an existing merge commit and skip re-rebasing, or document that a hand-merge must be pushed directly rather than re-run through `ship.py`.

**Found a real residual bug in that file's own same-day fix.** This morning's `f32b369c8` wrapped the IMAP connection (`imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(...)`) in try/except after it crashed `service_emails()` with `ssl.SSLEOFError`, aborting `--send`, the step that forwards Virtual Home Consult, In-Home Reset Day and Corporate Lean 6S enquiries. But `login()`, `select()`, `search()` and `fetch()` still sat in a bare `try/finally` with no `except`, one line below the fix: a bad password, a mid-session drop, or a timeout during search/fetch would crash the same function the same way. Widened the try/except around the whole IMAP conversation so any failure returns `None` (unchecked, not empty), matching `recent_service_charges()`'s own convention. New test, `check_imap_mid_session_failure_does_not_crash`, fakes a connection that opens fine and fails on `login()`; fail-then-pass proved directly (`git stash` on the source fix: new test failed by name with the real exception; restored: clean). Ledger updated.

**That check led into a full `preflight.py` run, which surfaced a second, unrelated real defect: two gates can FAIL on a scratch file that was never a page.** `gate_footer_consistent` and `gate_page_ownership_registry` both glob `site/` directly (one through `all_pages()`, one through a bare `glob.glob`) without skipping a leading underscore. `ops/audit_catalog.py`'s own `site/_audit_catalog_fixture_<pid>.html` is a gitignored, self-cleaning test probe, planted and removed around a lockdir precisely so a concurrent reader never sees a half-written copy; this run caught one genuinely on disk (left by a test my own verification sweep killed mid-section with too short a timeout) and both gates reported it as a real defect, "missing a footer entirely" and "unclassified page", on a file that was never shipped. `ops/wire_landmarks.py --check` has the identical gap (a third, separate glob with no underscore skip) and would fail the same way. `all_pages()`'s own docstring already names the fix (filter locally per caller, precedent `gate_roadmap_prices_current`); these three callers had not been updated to match. Fixed all three with the same `startswith("_")` skip. Ledgered both files.

## Addendum, 2026-10-03: closed the gap at the generator, and found my own verification method had been silently trusting itself

**Did:** Chained `build_seo.build_sitemap()` into `ops/build_zone_pages.py`'s `main()`, matching the pattern `build_corporate.py` and `build_resources.py` already use, so a standalone run after a `content.json` edit (the way every `common_items` cycle today reached for this file) can no longer leave the sitemap stale. This is CLAUDE.md step 10b: the same defect class had now shipped CI-red twice in one day, so the fix belongs in the generator, not in a third STATUS.md note.

**A real defect in how I was checking my own work, found while proving this one.** Calling `preflight.gate_sitemap_lastmod_current()` directly and catching `SystemExit` to mean "it passed" proves nothing: `fail()` only appends to a module-level `FAIL` list, and only `preflight.py`'s own `main()` turns that into a nonzero exit. Every gate I had called that way earlier this cycle looked clean whether it actually was or not. Caught it by building a proper fail-then-pass proof in an isolated worktree (`git worktree add`): reverted the fix, edited a zone's `common_items`, rebuilt, and the gate's real `FAIL` list came back empty even though the content had genuinely changed and the hash file had not, until I checked `preflight.FAIL` directly instead of trusting the absence of an exception, at which point it correctly named the stale URL. Re-checked the real repo's current state the correct way immediately afterward: still clean, so the Dining Room push earlier this cycle was in fact fine, but by luck of the underlying state being correct, not because my check would have caught it if it hadn't been.

**Verified:** fail-then-pass proved directly in the worktree (FAIL list populated naming the file, then empty after the fix). In the real repo: a full rebuild is idempotent (no diff), `check_urls.py` 211/211, `audit_pages.py` 215/0, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `test_gate_sitemap_lastmod_current.py` 6/6.

**Changing next cycle: verify every gate by reading `preflight.FAIL`/`preflight.WARN` after calling it, never by catching an exception that the function was never going to raise.** Recording this because CLAUDE.md 0.4 says exactly this class of mistake, an unchecked result silently standing in for a passing one, is the one that has cost the most here, and this was a live instance of it inside a single session, not a historical one.

**Next:** continue `common_items` room by room (Guest Bedroom or Guest Bathroom next); confirm `checks.yml` is green on this push and the two before it.

Pushed to main. `ops/build_zone_pages.py` only. No price or product touched, no new page.

**Found a real, live defect in `ops/dashboard.py`, a few hours after the cross-month revenue fix (`934510664`) shipped.** That fix correctly stopped relabelling a prior month's carried revenue as this month's, and renders "last known monthly figure: $X, measured &lt;date&gt;" instead. Its own `carry_forward()` sets the customer-count equivalent (`customers_last_measured`/`customers_measured_at`) in the same cross-month branch, but the renderer never read it: the `if S["revenue_month"] is None:` branch unconditionally wrote `S["customers_text"] = "not measured"`, discarding the carried figure outright. That is the exact "two headline figures contradict each other" shape `carry_forward()`'s own docstring names as the reason the customer carry-forward exists at all (its prior fix was for the same contradiction, revenue carried and the count not) — the sibling fix just re-opened a narrower version of it one field over.

**Fixed.** Extracted the whole revenue/customers rendering block (previously bare module-level code) into a new pure function, `revenue_customers_display(S)`, so it is testable the same way `carry_forward()` already is; the extraction is behavior-preserving (confirmed: dashboard output byte-identical for the same-month and never-measured cases before and after). The cross-month branch of the render now shows the carried customer count with its own "last known: N, measured &lt;date&gt;" caveat instead of discarding it. New `gate_dashboard_customers_text_reflects_carry` in `preflight.py`, the same synthetic-input pattern as the sibling `gate_dashboard_revenue_month_not_cross_month`; fail-then-pass proved directly by planting the old unconditional-"not measured" line, watching the gate fail by name citing the discarded figure, restoring, and reconfirming clean. `ops/tests/test_carry_forward.py` extended 15 to 18 cases the same way.

**Verified.** `check_urls.py` (211/211), `audit_pages.py` (215/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents), `fix_dashes.py --check` (0/0), `link_graph_report.py` (0 orphans), mobile `npm test` (all suites) all clean after. Both stale ledger entries closed with fresh notes naming today's actual findings (`ops/cold_read_ledger.py --stale` now reports 0).
